research_question: When does collecting more abundance samples help interaction prediction more than measuring additional interaction labels?
closest_prior_work: SPIEC-EASI and OneNet evaluate network inference across sample sizes; quantitative microbiome benchmarking studies examine measurement transformations. The current LENS experiment varies interaction labels with the abundance table held fixed.
proposed_gap: Evaluate a joint grid of abundance sample counts and experimental label counts on identical tested pairs. Estimate whether labels compensate for limited abundance information or whether inference remains constrained by the abundance data. This extends label-budget analysis without changing the model.
novelty_status: Provisional. Sample-size effects and label learning curves are established separately. A joint evaluation against real experimental outcomes may be useful but a comprehensive novelty audit is still needed; likely a LENS extension before a standalone paper.
available_data: Existing local LENS abundance and tested-pair tables for Butyrate Carlstrom and Schafer; Clark 2021 public study provides a source for synthetic gut assembly data. No new downloads required for an initial audit.
data_and_label_limitations: Abundance samples may share experimental conditions or contribute to the interaction labels themselves. Subsampling cannot represent independent acquisition unless provenance permits it. Taxa lost from a subset must not silently change the test universe. These tables are not interchangeable sequencing-count datasets.
minimal_experiment: After a provenance audit use a small prespecified grid of nested abundance subsets and label budgets with the frozen LENS architecture. Refit score generators for each abundance subset without labels; compute features from that subset only. Evaluate paired differences on fixed test pairs and record failures and fallback use.
baselines: Each individual score generator at the same abundance sample count; equal mean reference; LENS at each label budget. Include OneNet only if external refits are affordable and preserve its settings. Report AP and AUROC separately by system.
validation_design: Keep test pair identities and labels fixed across both budget axes. Group abundance subsampling by independent biological units where required and preserve planned experimental strata. Keep label selection independent of outcomes. Restrict preprocessing and tuning to permitted data. If abundance and truth share measurements describe the analysis as retrospective sensitivity rather than prospective acquisition guidance.
feasibility: A small pilot is feasible with local data but repeated network fitting adds computation. Start with one system and few abundance subsets only after approval. Compare sample and label counts first; financial conclusions require actual assay cost ratios.
main_risk: Dependence between abundance measurements and truth may invalidate an acquisition interpretation. Results may add only a sensitivity analysis to LENS. Many estimator refits could cost time without a distinct scientific contribution.
next_step: Audit whether the abundance rows and experimental truth can be separated by biological replicate or experiment; inspect prior network benchmarks for joint sample and label budgets before proposing a run.

research_question: Under a fixed assay budget should researchers measure more distinct microbial pairs or repeat measurements of uncertain pairs?
field: Experimental design for microbial interaction prediction
closest_prior_work: Replication or exploration? studies this allocation in stochastic simulation. A 2025 Scientific Reports study applies Bayesian active learning to genetic interaction discovery and explicitly represents repeated observations. Buyanbadrakh et al. 2026 reports replicated microbial spent medium growth assays.
proposed_gap: Evaluate the tradeoff between coverage of distinct pairs and precision of measured effects using real microbial assay replicates. Compare allocation rules at equal numbers of assay wells and controls while keeping prediction models and test pairs fixed. This concerns acquisition allocation; RG002 concerns changing outcome definitions.
novelty_status: Provisional. Replication allocation and active learning are established. A microbial evaluation with explicit assay accounting may be useful; no claim of a new general algorithm or first application.
available_data: Buyanbadrakh growth data are public in Zenodo record 17456178 with supplementary tables and public analysis code. Methods state that each condition was tested at least in duplicate. No files downloaded; usable independent replicate counts remain unverified.
data_and_label_limitations: Duplicate wells may be technical replicates with shared inocula and controls. Time points within one growth curve are not independent assays. Two replicates may be insufficient to estimate noise or emulate repeated acquisition. Spent medium effects differ from coculture effects.
minimal_experiment: First audit replicate and plate identifiers. If adequate, reserve whole test pairs and their measurements; compare more distinct training pairs with fewer repeatedly assayed training pairs at equal well budgets. Use a small fixed regression model and recompute training effect estimates using only revealed replicates. Evaluate continuous effect error and AP under a fixed biological effect definition.
baselines: Uniform pair selection with fixed replication; broad pair coverage with minimum permitted replication; uniform additional replication; an uncertainty-based allocation rule using only observed training measurements. Include all monoculture and control wells in the budget.
validation_design: Keep test pairs identical across allocation strategies and keep their outcomes hidden from selection. Group shared controls and biological batches where possible. Never reuse a revealed training replicate in reference test outcomes. Show sensitivity to technical versus biological replication; label retrospective allocation results as such.
feasibility: Potentially inexpensive with summary replicate tables and small models. Raw public file is about 1.1 GB and should not be downloaded before checking whether supplementary summaries suffice. A pilot is conditional on sufficient independent replication.
main_risk: The public replication structure may not support the proposed comparison; apparent gains could reflect shared controls or technical noise. General sequential design literature may already cover the methodological contribution.
next_step: Inspect supplementary metadata and the genetic interaction allocation method before running anything. Reject the pilot if independent replicates and control accounting cannot be reconstructed.

research_question: How much microbial interaction prediction comes from general sender and receiver tendencies instead of information specific to a pair?
closest_prior_work: Khatbane et al. 2025 KGEMI already compared sender and receiver majority-class baselines on Kehe data. Nestor et al. 2023 used growth and phylogeny. A 2025 GNN preprint compared graph learning with XGBoost.
proposed_gap: Initially considered an audit using regularized sender and receiver effects plus environment effects and testing the incremental value of pair features across label budgets. The broad claim that organism tendencies need a baseline is already addressed in KGEMI.
novelty_status: Not established as a new gap. Direct prior work overlaps substantially; deprioritize as a separate paper unless a fuller audit identifies a consequential missing comparison.
available_data: Public Nestor code and data repository and the Kehe experimental resource reused by KGEMI. Repository availability checked; files not downloaded or audited.
data_and_label_limitations: Pairs share strains and environments. Missing measurements are not neutral labels. An identity model can interpolate among observed strains but requires a defined fallback for unseen strains.
minimal_experiment: Only if revived: compare a joint additive regularized model with separate sender and receiver baselines and a growth model on fixed tests at matched label budgets. Measure the gain from adding pair features. No analysis run today.
baselines: KGEMI sender and receiver class baselines; class frequencies; joint additive logistic model with shrinkage; growth-based XGBoost; published graph estimator only if reproducible.
validation_design: Group reciprocal pairs and replicates. Separate withheld pairs among observed strains from withheld strains and environments. Estimate all organism tendencies from training labels only. Report per-class AP and continuous-effect error where effects are available; do not equate high accuracy with pair-specific biological learning.
feasibility: Small additive models should be inexpensive. Reproducing complex graph methods may add setup work; public summary tables could support a pilot.
main_risk: Likely an incremental baseline check rather than a defensible standalone contribution. Existing null models already cover the central motivation.
next_step: Do not start a new experiment. Retain as a possible baseline check when reviewing KGEMI methods and supplements in full.

research_question: Can measurements of pH and individual growth reduce the number of interaction experiments needed to predict effects after nutrient replenishment?
closest_prior_work: Ratzke and Gore 2018 established pH modification and sensitivity as interaction mechanisms. Buyanbadrakh et al. 2026 measured 1224 directional combinations using 36 gut strains in spent and replenished media and already predicted spent medium effects from pH.
proposed_gap: Test the value of individual physiological measurements for adaptation between conditions at fixed interaction label budgets. Measure when a few target condition labels improve a frozen physiological predictor. The contribution would be a measurement tradeoff and transfer evaluation.
novelty_status: Provisional. Prediction from pH is established; a new feature combination alone is insufficient. A focused audit of budget and transfer studies remains necessary.
available_data: Buyanbadrakh supplementary data include growth effects and pH assays. Public Zenodo raw_data.csv is 1.1 GB; public GitHub provides Analysis.R. No data downloaded.
data_and_label_limitations: Spent medium assays are directional growth effects and cannot substitute for a complete abundance network benchmark. Replenishment changes nutrients and pH together. Replicate alignment and overlapping usable pairs need verification; selected pH rescue experiments may be biased.
minimal_experiment: Use summary tables first. Predict continuous effects with a small ridge model from donor pH and recipient growth response to pH. Compare source condition training alone with increasing target condition labels. Evaluate on identical hidden target pairs; retain a separate analysis of unobserved strains.
baselines: Published pH predictor; donor and recipient means; growth-only ridge; target-only ridge; source-only ridge; source model with a regularized target update. Compare error for continuous effects and AP for prespecified inhibition labels.
validation_design: Group reciprocal pairs and replicates. Keep target tests fixed across budgets and separate shared-strain from excluded-strain tests. Fit transformations and penalties inside training data. Allow target physiology only when explicitly counted as available measurements. Count source labels and physiological assays as costs; do not claim savings from pair counts alone.
feasibility: A small retrospective pilot should be manageable using summary tables and R. No network refits needed. Actual time or financial savings would require laboratory cost information.
main_risk: The published physiological predictor may already answer most of the question. One assay family limits generalization. Target physiology can be expensive or inadvertently contain pair outcomes.
next_step: Audit supplementary tables 1 2 6 and 7 and the original prediction procedure; verify independent physiological inputs and matching conditions before deciding whether to run a pilot.

research_question: Do conclusions about microbial interaction predictors remain stable when the experimental definition of a neutral effect changes?
closest_prior_work: Kehe et al. 2021 measured cocultures across 20 soil strains and 40 carbon environments; Nestor et al. 2023 predicted interactions from growth; a 2024 flux balance evaluation defined neutral effects using growth ratios between 0.8 and 1.2; a 2025 knowledge graph study discretized measured effects into positive negative and neutral classes.
proposed_gap: Evaluate whether model ordering and class-specific predictive performance are robust to prespecified biologically plausible neutral intervals and assay detection rules on the same measured pairs. Distinguish effects of changing class frequency from changes in which pairs are labeled.
novelty_status: Provisional; neither threshold sensitivity nor three-class prediction is new. A systematic comparison of robustness to experimental label definitions may be useful but absence from existing work is not established.
available_data: Kehe supplementary Data S1 and Nestor public code/data repository; 2024 flux balance evaluation reports experimental inputs from six studies. Public availability statements verified; raw contents and replicate completeness not audited.
data_and_label_limitations: Aggregated effect tables may lack replicate measurements or limits of detection. Do not turn nonsignificant tests into established biological absence. Do not pool assay types or opposite directions. The many Kehe measurements include replication and are not independent pairs.
minimal_experiment: Audit one continuous coculture effect table; reproduce its original labels; prespecify a small set of alternative neutral intervals from assay precision or prior literature; use identical hidden pair groups for all definitions; compare a growth-only logistic model and XGBoost with a continuous-effect regression approach. Keep ambiguous measurements recorded and analyze exclusions explicitly.
baselines: Majority and class-frequency references; sender and receiver frequency baselines; growth-only logistic regression; XGBoost; regression with prespecified effect cutoffs. Report per-class AP and macro F1 with class counts rather than only accuracy.
validation_design: Group reciprocal effects and replicates; keep outer folds and test membership fixed across label definitions; tune models within training folds only; set neutral rules without test performance. Report both fixed-score relabeling sensitivity and retrained-model sensitivity. Use grouped uncertainty and show prevalence beside AP; do not interpret an AP change from relabeling alone as a model improvement.
feasibility: Potentially inexpensive with public tables and small models; no abundance network refits are required for a first pilot. Replicate-based extension depends on data availability.
main_risk: Could be a sensitivity section rather than a standalone paper; existing studies may already perform the same audit; arbitrary cutoffs would weaken the contribution; model order could remain unchanged.
next_step: Inspect the original label equations and supplementary sensitivity analyses in the 2024 flux balance and 2025 knowledge graph papers; audit whether Kehe or Nestor releases continuous effects and uncertainty before running anything.

research_question: Can selective prediction identify reliable microbial interaction predictions when experimental labels are scarce and test strains or environments differ from training?
closest_prior_work: Nestor et al. 2023 predicts interaction signs from growth with organism and environment exclusion tests; Rubrice et al. 2025 predicts biofilm antagonism with homology-controlled validation and discusses conformal uncertainty; Ding et al. 2024 controls false discoveries in enzyme annotation.
proposed_gap: Measure the tradeoff between prediction error and the fraction of predictions retained as label budgets decrease under shared-strain and excluded-strain or excluded-environment evaluation; assess whether uncertainty offers value beyond simple confidence thresholds.
novelty_status: Provisional candidate only; selective and conformal prediction are established and microbial antagonism work already overlaps. No claim of first application. A broader related-work audit is required.
available_data: Nestor public code/data repository; Rubrice public code and biofilm data repository; existing LENS data as a separate optional application.
data_and_label_limitations: Repeated pairs share organisms and conditions; assay outcomes differ; neutral labels cannot be invented for signed-only data; rare classes limit calibration; code/data availability verified from public pages but files not downloaded or audited.
minimal_experiment: Use one fixed logistic or ridge model; allocate separate training and uncertainty-calibration labels within each budget; compare confidence rejection and class-conditional conformal sets; evaluate retained-prediction error and retained fraction per class on fixed hidden tests. Begin with one public system and add an independent assay only if compatible.
baselines: Predict every pair; reject by maximum class probability; reject by estimator disagreement; standard split conformal; class-conditional conformal; simple growth predictor where available. Match total label budgets and report rejection of rare outcomes.
validation_design: Keep reciprocal measurements and replicates grouped; separate random pair interpolation from strain and environment exclusion; keep test identities fixed across budgets; tune rejection only on training/calibration data. Report empirical coverage and error with dependence-aware uncertainty; do not claim exchangeability-based guarantees under biological shift or conflate conformal coverage with false discovery control.
feasibility: Potentially manageable with small models and public tables; no new wet lab work required for retrospective evaluation. Exact sample counts and compute requirements require a data audit.
main_risk: Strong overlap with the 2025 biofilm study; abstention may reject nearly every rare outcome; selective accuracy alone can look good by retaining only easy neutral pairs; retrospective results do not establish actual cost savings.
next_step: Read the complete Rubrice uncertainty methods and inspect the Nestor data schema before deciding whether the proposed budget and shift evaluation is genuinely missing.
